episodes.176903: A closed upper low pressure system produced light to moderate rainfall, isolated thunderstorms and light snow in the mountains February 12 to 13, with most of the impacts felt in San Diego County. The heaviest and most widespread rain occurred from the coastal slopes towards the coast in San Diego County, where isolated lightning was observed. Also, light snow was reported in the mountains in San Diego County and Riverside County.
episodes.177047: A low pressure system encountered deep moisture while tracking across southeast South Carolina, helping produce light to moderate showers and strong gradient winds across the region.
episodes.178280: Isolated convective rain showers developed well in advance of a strong cold front approaching from the southeast Gulf of Mexico.  Isolated gale-force wind gusts occurred with the showers south of Marathon, Florida.

events.narrative: The South Carolina Highway Patrol reported roadway flooding near the intersection of Orangeburg Road and Williams Family Drive. Broadcast media also reported a section of Orangeburg Road between US 17A and Dorchester Road closed due to part of the road being washed out near a construction zone.

events.county: Hawk Channel From Craig Key To West End Of Seven Mile Bridge Out To The Reef
events.narrative: A west wind gust of 40 knots was measured at the new Sombrero Key Light .

Widespread rainfall occurred on the afternoon and evening of February 12, developing across the coastal mountain slopes and moving westward towards the coast in San Diego County. Lightning was reported across coastal areas as well as the deserts. The heaviest rainfall occurred across the valleys where general 0.50-0.75 were reported, with the highest amount of 1.39 recorded at Harbison Canyon.
